Q: What are some key events and characters from [Genesis 1-11](https://servewell.net/-/Genesis/1)?
A: Creation, Adam and Eve, the Fall, Cain and Abel, the Flood, Babel. If you knew others, you should get bonus points!

Q: What significant couple died at around 2000 BCE (give or take)?
A: According to some traditional chronologies, Sarah died at around 2029 and Abraham died at around 1991. Their story is found in the book of [Genesis chapters 12-25](https://servewell.net/-/Genesis/12).

Q: What biblical book, likely set in a time before the Exodus though its date of composition is uncertain, wrestles with the question of why a righteous person suffers?
What five documents are known as the Pentateuch, the Torah, or the books of Moses?
What significant events happened 1446-1380 BCE (give or take a few hundred years)?
A: The departure or exodus of the Israelites from Egypt, led by Moses, and their entry into the Promised Land, led by Joshua. Dates are debated. This story is found in [Exodus](https://servewell.net/-/Exodus/1) through [Joshua](https://servewell.net/-/Joshua/1).

Q: What short narrative book tells the story of a Moabite woman who remained loyal to her Hebrew mother-in-law and became an ancestor of King David?
What significant period occurred around 1380–1050 BCE?
A: The period of the Judges, in which the Israelites were ruled by a series of local rulers or judges before the establishment of the monarchy. This story is found in the books of [Judges](https://servewell.net/-/Judges/1), [Ruth](https://servewell.net/-/Ruth/1) and part of [1 Samuel](https://servewell.net/-/1-Samuel/1).

Q: What Hebrew king's reign started around 1050 BCE?
A: Saul. The story of Saul is found in [1 Samuel chapters 9-31](https://servewell.net/-/1-Samuel/9).

Q: What Hebrew king's reign over all Israel started around 1000 BCE?
A: David. The story of David is found in [1 Samuel chapters 16-31](https://servewell.net/-/1-Samuel/16), [2 Samuel](https://servewell.net/-/2-Samuel/1) and [1 Chronicles](https://servewell.net/-/1-Chronicles/1).

Q: What large collection of songs and prayers was compiled over many centuries and used in Israelite worship?
What Hebrew king's reign started around 971 BCE?
A: Solomon. The story of Solomon is found in [1 Kings chapters 1-11](https://servewell.net/-/1-Kings/1) and [2 Chronicles chapters 1-9](https://servewell.net/-/2-Chronicles/1).

Q: What book of wisdom sayings is primarily associated with King Solomon, though it draws from multiple sources?
What book, traditionally attributed to Solomon, reflects on the meaning and limits of human endeavor, wealth, and wisdom?
What book of lyrical poetry, attributed to Solomon, celebrates love and marriage?
A: [Song of Songs](https://servewell.net/-/Song-of-Songs/1) (also called Song of Solomon or Canticles).

Q: What significant events happened around 931 BCE?
A: Solomon died, his son Rehoboam began to rule over the united kingdom of twelve tribes, and then most of the tribes left and appointed Jeroboam as their king in the north, resulting in two kingdoms for a few hundred years. The story is in [1 Kings 12](https://servewell.net/-/1-Kings/12) and [2 Chronicles 10](https://servewell.net/-/2-Chronicles/10).

Q: What minor prophetic document of unknown date describes plagues and contrasts them with the outpouring of God's Spirit?
What minor prophetic document, by a farmer from Judah, delivered a message of judgment to the Northern Kingdom of Israel around 760–750 BCE, during the prosperous reign of Jeroboam II?

What substantial but officially minor prophetic document, which uses the metaphor of an unfaithful marriage to describe Israel's unfaithfulness, comes from the Northern Kingdom of Israel in the decades before 722 BCE?
What minor prophetic document tells of a prophet sent to call the Assyrian city of Nineveh to repentance, and is traditionally placed in the time of Jeroboam II (~760–750 BCE)?
A: [Jonah](https://servewell.net/-/Jonah/1). The prophet is mentioned in [2 Kings 14:25](https://servewell.net/-/2-Kings/14#25).

Q: What significant event happened around 722–721 BCE?
A: The Neo-Assyrian army, led by King Shalmaneser V in 722 and then by his successor Sargon II in 721, conquered the Northern Kingdom of Israel and its capital, Samaria. This resulted in the mass deportation of Israelites into exile. The story is in [2 Kings 17](https://servewell.net/-/2-Kings/17).

Q: What significant event happened around 701 BCE?
A: The Neo-Assyrian army, led by King Sennacherib, invaded Judah (the southern kingdom) but did not destroy Jerusalem. This event is mentioned in [2 Kings 18](https://servewell.net/-/2-Kings/18#13) and [2 Chronicles 32](https://servewell.net/-/2-Chronicles/32#1).

Q: What major prophetic document comes from a prophet who served in Judah around 739–680 BCE?
A: [Isaiah](https://servewell.net/-/Isaiah/1). The prophet is mentioned for example in [2 Kings 19:20](https://servewell.net/-/2-Kings/19#20).

Q: What minor prophetic document comes from a contemporary of Isaiah in Judah around 735–700 BCE, and predicts that Bethlehem would be the birthplace of a great ruler?
What minor prophetic document predicted the fall of Nineveh that happened around 612 BCE?
A: [Nahum](https://servewell.net/-/Nahum/1). Nineveh, the Assyrian capital, fell to an allied force led by the Babylonians.

Q: What minor prophetic document comes from a prophet who served in Judah during the reign of King Josiah around 640–620 BCE and starts with catastrophic apocalyptic language?
What minor prophetic document addressed the rising Babylonian threat to Judah around 610–597 BCE?
What significant events happened around 605 BCE?
A: The Babylonian army under King Nebuchadnezzar defeated Egypt at the Battle of Carchemish and then forced King Jehoiakim of Jerusalem into submission, and took some Hebrew nobles captive to Babylon. This event is mentioned in [2 Kings 24:1](https://servewell.net/-/2-Kings/24#1) and [Jeremiah 46:2](https://servewell.net/-/Jeremiah/46#2).

Q: What major prophetic document focuses on a man who was exiled to Babylon in 605 BCE and went on to become a high-profile leader?
A: [Daniel](https://servewell.net/-/Daniel/1). The deportation event is mentioned in [Daniel 1:1-6](https://servewell.net/-/Daniel/1#1-6).

Q: What significant events happened around 597 BCE?
A: The Babylonian army, again under King Nebuchadnezzar, took King Jehoiachin and thousands of prominent citizens as captives to Babylon. This event is mentioned in [2 Kings 24:10-17](https://servewell.net/-/2-Kings/24#10) and [Jeremiah 52:28-30](https://servewell.net/-/Jeremiah/52#28).

Q: What major prophetic document covers the ministry of a prophet exiled to Babylon in 597 BCE?
A: [Ezekiel](https://servewell.net/-/Ezekiel/1). The beginning of Ezekiel's ministry a few years later is introduced in [Ezekiel 1:1-3](https://servewell.net/-/Ezekiel/1#1-3).

Q: What significant events happened around 586 BCE?
A: The Babylonian army, again under King Nebuchadnezzar, destroyed Jerusalem and took most remaining Hebrews captive to Babylon. This event is mentioned in [2 Kings 25](https://servewell.net/-/2-Kings/25) and [2 Chronicles 36:15-21](https://servewell.net/-/2-Chronicles/36#15).

Q: What major prophetic document comes from a prophet who was active in the midst of the events of 586 BCE?
What biblical document is often included in the Major Prophets section mourning the events of 586 BCE?
A: [Lamentations](https://servewell.net/-/Lamentations/1). This book is traditionally attributed to the prophet Jeremiah.

Q: What minor prophetic document delivered a message of judgment against Edom for rejoicing over the events of 586 BCE?
What significant event happened around 539 BCE?
A: The Persian army under King Cyrus the Great conquered Babylon, which led to the end of the Babylonian exile for the Hebrews. This event is mentioned in [2 Chronicles 36:22-23](https://servewell.net/-/2-Chronicles/36#22) and [Ezra 1:1-4](https://servewell.net/-/Ezra/1#1).

Q: What two minor prophetic documents, from around 520–518 BCE, called the returned exiles to resume rebuilding the Jerusalem temple and encouraged them with visions of God's future purposes?
A: [Haggai](https://servewell.net/-/Haggai/1) and [Zechariah](https://servewell.net/-/Zechariah/1). Haggai is precisely dated to the second year of King Darius (520 BCE).

Q: What significant event happened around 516 BCE?
A: The Second Temple in Jerusalem was completed and dedicated. This event is mentioned in [Ezra 6:15-18](https://servewell.net/-/Ezra/6#15).

Q: What narrative book, set in the Persian court around 480 BCE, tells the story of a Jewish woman who became queen and helped save her people from destruction?
What narrative book tells the story of a Jewish official who returned to Jerusalem to rebuild its walls and reform the community around 445-430 BCE?
What significant milestone is believed to have happened around 430 BCE?
A: The last of the Old Testament prophets, [Malachi](https://servewell.net/-/Malachi/1), is believed to have completed his ministry around this time. This is based on the content of the book of Malachi and its historical context, although the exact date is debated among scholars.

Q: What significant conquest happened around 332 BCE?
A: Alexander the Great of Macedon conquered the Persian Empire, which included the land of the Hebrews. This led to the Hellenistic period in the region in which Greek became a dominant language. The story is not directly mentioned in the Bible, but it sets the stage for events in the intertestamental period and the New Testament.

Q: What significant event happened around 63 BCE?
A: The Roman general Pompey conquered Jerusalem, which led to Roman rule over the region. This event is not directly mentioned in the Bible, but it sets the stage for the political context of the New Testament.

Q: What significant event happened around 4 BCE?
A: The birth of Jesus Christ. The exact year of Jesus' birth is debated among scholars, but it is commonly placed around 4 BCE based on historical and biblical evidence.

Q: What significant events happened around 26–33 CE?
A: The ministry, crucifixion, resurrection and ascension of Jesus Christ and the beginning of the Christian church. The exact dates are debated, but these dates are based on historical and biblical evidence. The story is found in the four Gospels: [Matthew](https://servewell.net/-/Matthew/1), [Mark](https://servewell.net/-/Mark/1), [Luke](https://servewell.net/-/Luke/1) and [John](https://servewell.net/-/John/1) and in the book of [Acts](https://servewell.net/-/Acts/1).

Q: What document narrates the spread of the early church from Jerusalem outward, covering roughly 33–62 CE?
What letter, possibly the earliest New Testament document, is attributed to a brother of Jesus and emphasizes that genuine faith must produce practical action?
What two letters of Paul are among the earliest New Testament writings, addressed to a young church in Greece around 50–51 CE and touching on Christ's return?
What letter of Paul, addressed to the church in a major commercial city in Greece, is the longest of his letters and covers topics including spiritual gifts, love, and resurrection?
What letter of Paul defends his apostleship and expresses his deep concern for a church he had founded in Greece?
What letter of Paul, addressed to churches in a region that is now part of Türkiye, combats teachers who were insisting that Gentile believers must be circumcised and keep the Mosaic law?

What letter of Paul, considered by many his most systematic presentation of the gospel, addresses divisions likely caused by the separation of Jewish and Gentile believers that was enforced by the Emperor Claudius?
What four letters of Paul are traditionally grouped as ‘prison letters,’ written while he was under Roman custody?
What three letters of Paul are grouped as ‘pastoral letters,’ addressed to individuals rather than congregations, giving guidance on church leadership and conduct?
What two letters are attributed to a leading apostle, the first offering encouragement to scattered believers under persecution and the second warning against false teachers?
What anonymous document addresses covenant transition?
What letters are attributed to an apostle of love, the longer one focusing on the nature of God as light and love?
What letter is attributed to a lesser-known brother of Jesus and warns against false teaching that had crept into the church?
What significant event happened around 70 CE?
A: The destruction of the Second Temple in Jerusalem by the Roman army under General Titus. This event is mentioned in [Luke 21:20-24](https://servewell.net/-/Luke/21#20-24) and [Matthew 24:1-2](https://servewell.net/-/Matthew/24#1-2).

Q: What document includes messages for seven churches in the area now known as western Türkiye?
